WHAT_IS_CONFIRMED: The non-carrier GO_HOME legality defect is repaired. This is recorded as an independently successful interface repair, separable from Repair A (DEFEND primitive), which came back PARTIAL for unrelated reasons.

THE_DEFECT.symptom: G6_LEGALITY failed for exactly one candidate in the entire suite: ATTACK_HOME_TEAMMATE_CARRIER / GO_HOME_NONCARRIER, declared structurally_satisfiable=false.
THE_DEFECT.what_was_already_correct: That candidate's behavior was already exact before any repair: G6_TARGET 0.000 cells, G6_DIRECTION cosine 1.000 and radial agreement 1.000, G6_TRAJECTORY 1.313 cells (inside the 2.5 threshold). Three of four sub-gates passed. Only selectability failed.
THE_DEFECT.root_cause_verified_in_the_engine: The engine never blocked this. gpu_env/_core/_step.py::_advance_blue_macros accepts any macro id unconditionally (torch.remainder against n_macros); there is no carrying precondition on macro selection anywhere. The false declaration reflected only that GO_HOME's own capture-success flag -- blue_cap_agents = prev_carrying & ~carrying & cap_env, gpu_env/_core/_step.py -- cannot fire for an agent that is not the carrier.
THE_DEFECT.why_that_was_the_wrong_criterion: Capture-eligibility is the completion semantics of the literal flag-carrier. For a non-carrying escort assigned to follow the carrier home, correctness is target/direction/trajectory fidelity, which was already exact. Requiring a capture event that was never this agent's to trigger conflated two different questions.

THE_REPAIR.scope: One boolean, read in exactly one branch of gpu_env/pyquaticus_port.py::projection_candidates.
THE_REPAIR.changes: structurally_satisfiable for the GO_HOME_NONCARRIER candidate only
does_not_change: the sibling GO_TO_HOME_WAYPOINT_NONCARRIER candidate (verified byte-identical with the flag on and off)
any production engine code -- no change was needed, because no engine restriction existed

EVIDENCE.C4_orthogonality: B_fixes_home_legality PASS, B_does_not_touch_target PASS, A_does_not_touch_legality PASS, attack_to_flag_unaffected_everywhere PASS.
EVIDENCE.independence_from_repair_A: The DEFEND_OFF/HOME_ON combination shows the single legality fix with a G6_TARGET fail list identical to DEFEND_OFF/HOME_OFF. The DEFEND_ON/HOME_OFF combination shows the identical DEFEND target failure with the legality fail list unchanged. The two repairs provably do not interact.
EVIDENCE.C2_legacy_preservation: With both flags off, every metric in every case/candidate reproduces the sealed PYQUATICUS_PORT_CONTRACT_RESULT.json with zero mismatches, and that sealed file's sha256 was verified unchanged before and after the sweep.
EVIDENCE.tests: tests/test_pyquaticus_port_contracts.py::test_repair_home_legality_flips_only_the_satisfiability_flag asserts the flag changes only satisfiability, leaving macro, target_index and the sibling candidate identical. 33 tests in that file pass, including all 14 that predate the repair.

DEPLOYMENT_CONSTRAINT.default_off: The flag stays default-OFF. It is not globally enabled.
DEPLOYMENT_CONSTRAINT.explicitly_not_retroactive: No prior experiment, sealed result, checkpoint, preset or training run is re-run, re-scored or re-interpreted under this repair. Every historical artifact keeps the semantics it was produced under.
DEPLOYMENT_CONSTRAINT.opt_in_only: Any future experiment wanting this behavior must enable the flag explicitly and say so in its own frozen spec.

CLAIM_BOUNDARY: This confirms one action-interface legality defect is repaired, in an outcome-blind CPU contract on fixed fixtures. It establishes nothing about learned specialization, PPO, team payoff, the 4v4 B failure, or whether escort behavior matters to any outcome. It does not unblock the Pyquaticus team evaluation, which remains gated on DEFEND representability.
